LESSON: MULTIPLICATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.5: Multiplication
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Multiplication, part of Numbers in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can you work out multiplication using repeated addition? 2. How do you model multiplication as repeated addition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. model multiplication as repeated addition using numbers 1,2,3,4 and 5 by 4 and 5,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Multiplication in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. multiply a single digit number by a single digit number,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Multiplication in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. multiply single digit numbers by 10,

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Multiplication together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: learner discovers the connection between repeated addition of numbers and multiplication.

● Creativity and imagination: learner models multiplication as repeated addition of numbers.

Values:
• Respect: learner appreciates others as they take turns to practise multiplication of a single digit numbers by 10 using

multiplication tables.

● Social justice: learner fosters fairness and justice among peers as they play games involving multiplication.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental conservation: learner re-uses improvised learning materials and objects such as charts and counters.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate skills used in playing games to performance skills in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning resources:

Bottle tops, marbles, stones, sticks, grains, print and braille multiplication tables, digital devices with assistive technology

such as screen reader, screen magnifiers and tactile keyboards.
